title: Human-in-the-Loop: Where Humans Actually Intervene
use_cases: Use when building a collaborative writing environment requiring human oversight
Implement when preventing continuity and coherence errors in long-form narratives
Configure when human approval is required before AI transitions from planning to content generation
Use when a workflow requires AI to propose drafts for human refinement
content:
“HIL” only matters if it’s concrete. Here’s how it works for us:

1. Artifacts creation (human-led, AI-assisted):Humans can write Story Bible / Starting Point / Checkpoint manually, or ask AI to propose drafts that the human edits.
2. Outline generation (AI)
3. Human review and edits:The author/editor reviews the outline output, adjusts pacing, adds constraints, corrects direction, and approves it.
4. Drafting Chapters (AI) from an approved outline
5. Optional human review of chapters.

So humans don’t only set the destination, they also approve the plan before the system writes prose.

This system is not bulletproof. It can and does break. But it’s a start, and it meaningfully reduces a large class of continuity and coherence errors that show up in long-form serialized generation.
